If you are new to Python or need help setting up your computer, the [step-by-step local setup guide](developer-setup.ipynb) explains the tools, installs the software, and helps you check that your workspace is ready. You do not need to have Python installed beforehand.

Choose where you want to work:

- [Local setup with VS Code](developer-setup.ipynb) keeps your files and Python environment on your computer. You need a supported computer and permission to install software; the guide lists compatible systems.
- [Google Colab setup](colab-setup.qmd) lets you work in a browser using Google's computers, without installing software locally. You need a Google account and an internet connection. Your notebook can be saved in Drive; computing sessions are temporary.
- [Slurm cluster setup with VS Code](slurm-setup.qmd) uses your institution's computing resources for work that needs them. You need a cluster account and its connection and resource-allocation details. The guide covers preparing a remote workspace and running notebooks on allocated resources.

If you already have a Python environment, use the installation commands below.

## Install the package

These instructions assume you already have a Python environment for your work. JAXCMR requires **Python 3.12 or later**. Activate your chosen environment before running either installation command below.

Install from GitHub to obtain the version covered by this documentation; the release on PyPI is older. These commands require [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads), which the installer uses to download the source. Required Python dependencies are installed automatically.

### With uv — recommended

We recommend [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) because it can manage Python versions, environments, and packages together. With uv installed, run:

```bash
uv pip install git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr
```

### With pip

If you prefer pip, install into your existing Python environment with:

```bash
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr
```

## Get the repository and examples

Cloning the repository gives you a local copy of JAXCMR's source code and example notebooks. The repository includes a configuration for setting up its Python environment with uv.

Install both [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), then run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr.git
cd jaxcmr
uv sync
```

`uv sync` downloads Python 3.12 if needed, creates a `.venv` environment, and installs JAXCMR and the notebook tools. Changes to JAXCMR's source files are available without reinstalling the package.
